summary: Backend-only validation of AI Outfit Generator + Smart Affiliate Engine endpoints. 26/26 pytest cases passed against the live preview backend, covering happy paths, auth enforcement, Mongo _id leakage, AI JSON parsing, click redirect tracking, and regression on /api/auth/login & /api/auth/me.

minor.issue: Endpoint is public and increments click counter on any anonymous GET request. Fraud check is only triggered when a clicker_user_id is present, so prefetchers / bots / link previewers (e.g. Slack, iMessage, antivirus URL scanners) will inflate clicks. Consider gating by User-Agent, requiring a session, or rate-limiting per IP.

Aggregation uses {created_at: {$gte: first-of-current-month}} comparing ISO strings. Works for current-year ISO strings but is brittle across years/timezones; safer to store BSON Date or use UTC ranges.

Both endpoints are unauthenticated and expose any user's affiliate links by outfit/post id. If outfit/post ids are guessable or referenced publicly elsewhere, this leaks per-user link data (retailer, search query, target URL). Consider requiring auth or filtering by ownership/visibility.

action_items: Consider adding bot/UA filtering or rate limit on /api/affiliate/track/{link_id} to avoid inflated click counts.
Decide whether /api/affiliate/outfit/{outfit_id} and /api/affiliate/post/{post_id} should require auth or filter by ownership.
Optional: persist created_at as BSON Date so /api/outfits/trending aggregation is timezone-safe.
critical_code_review_comments: outfit_generator._parse_outfit_response: when the AI returns non-JSON, the fallback constructs an outfit with items=[]. /api/outfits/generate then passes those (empty) items to affiliate_engine.suggest_for_items which short-circuits with []. End user gets a successful 200 but no items and no affiliate links. Consider returning a clearer error or retry-with-stricter-prompt path.
server.py is now 3322 lines. The new Outfit + Affiliate routes (~200 lines) should be moved into routers/outfits.py and routers/affiliate.py to keep the file under the 700-line guideline.

AffiliateEngine.track_click increments clicks via $inc but commits a click document even when 'suspicious'. Stats aggregation correctly ignores clicks counter for suspicious clicks, but the click document itself has no soft-delete; downstream reporting must filter on suspicious=False.
affiliate_engine.create_links iterates suggestions x retailers and inserts one document per pair without bulk_write — for 5–6 items this is ~12 round-trips. Use insert_many for better latency.
/api/affiliate/suggest accepts arbitrary items: List[Dict] with no schema validation. Add a Pydantic model (item, category, color all optional strings) to fail fast on malformed payloads.
test_credentials: testuser@looksy.com / test1234 / category=men (session cookie via POST /api/auth/login)
seed_data_creation: Tests created 1 new outfit + ~10 affiliate links + 1 style profile + 1 tracking click for testuser@looksy.com. All entries are scoped to that user and harmless.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run `pytest /app/backend/tests/test_outfit_affiliate.py -v` to re-validate. The OutfitGenerator's _parse_outfit_response fallback path (when AI returns non-JSON) is NOT covered by live tests — mock LlmChat if you want to exercise it. The track endpoint is public; in tests we use allow_redirects=False to inspect the 302 Location header. /app/memory/test_credentials.md is MISSING — main agent should create it with the testuser credentials.
